A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ITA/IEL research work. Their main text, equations, tables, proofs and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite restructuring and changes in notation and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original class-incremental experiments on seven datasets, including accuracy, forgetting, regularization ablations, specialization and unlearning results in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 reports original ITA/IEL experiments, revised benchmark and ablation results, an empirical-risk analysis, and expanded specialization and unlearning results in Section 5 and Appendix H.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains task pre-consolidation, accumulated diagonal Fisher information, individual versus composed-model training, and the regularization objectives in Equations 11–19. v2 explicitly documents initialization and local cross-entropy, but does not establish that these disclosures represent changes to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The seven class-incremental datasets remain unchanged. Specialization and unlearning coverage expands from ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100 and RESISC in v1 Table 2 to all seven datasets in v2 Table 7, extending these editing tasks to CUB-200, Caltech-256, MIT-67 and CropDiseases.

E2.justification: v2 adds InfLoRA as an evaluated comparator across all seven datasets, with accuracy, forgetting and standard-deviation entries in Tables 1, 4 and 5. The existing comparator set is otherwise retained, including TMC in the specialization and unlearning comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix I substantially revises reported settings relative to v1 Appendix G. Examples include ITA-LoRA's CropDisease pre-consolidation budget changing from 15 to 8 epochs, IEL-FFT's CIFAR-100 learning rate changing from 0.00001 to 0.0001, and IEL-LoRA's Caltech classifier regularization coefficient changing from 0.05 to 5. These establish changed reported configurations, without independently establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds a targeted diagnostic comparing the composed model's empirical risk, weighted individual-model risk and linear-probed pre-training risk, with and without regularization. v1 provides accuracy ablations but no corresponding risk-bound analysis. The existing regularization-removal and classifier-only ablation designs are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 5 first supplies standard deviations for the FFT and IA3 variants whose accuracy results already appeared in v1 Tables 3 and 6. Both versions retain three-repetition averaging; v2 describes 'three runs' instead of explicitly specifying 'three class orders.' No increase in repetitions or new significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Accuracy, forgetting, ablation and editing results are extensively revised. For example, ITA-LoRA's reported ImageNet-R accuracy changes from 78.43 to 77.79 and CUB-200 accuracy from 81.48 to 85.55; its CIFAR-100 unlearning target accuracy changes from 62.79 to 28.67. InfLoRA results, additional editing results and Figure 1's risk findings are added. Revised settings prevent treating these numerical changes as controlled performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 2 defines all-task empirical risk and transfers the central local-minimum, positive-semidefinite-Hessian and Jensen-bound argument to that risk. v1 assumes local optimality of the per-example loss before averaging its bound. This materially weakens a foundational assumption, although Theorem 1 and the appendix proofs and gradient derivations remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: a second-order account of nonlinear model compositionality, the importance of preserving pre-training knowledge, dual ITA/IEL algorithms, and compositional specialization and unlearning capabilities. The additional evidence and qualifications do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v1 interprets ITA's unlearning behavior as suggesting greater knowledge entanglement than TMC; v2 instead argues for more effective disentanglement. v2 also adds substantive discussion of Taylor-approximation validity under parameter drift, Gaussian and diagonal-Fisher approximations, and the absence of a guaranteed improvement over pre-training in Sections 5–6.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the exact timm checkpoint, initialization for FFT/LoRA/IA3, local cross-entropy and its application to competitors, and validation-based grid search using 10% of training data. Appendix I adds linear-probing learning rates, InfLoRA settings and CLS-prior coefficients. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's existing optimizer, Fisher-estimation and regularization details.

R1.justification: v2 adds InfLoRA positioning and a substantial Appendix F comparing initialization, regularization, composition and inference costs with existing methods. New literature supports the discussions of local cross-entropy, lazy training, loss geometry and curvature approximations. Some earlier continual-learning references are removed; the existing model-merging discussion is relocated rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the framework and algorithm explanations, places regularization analysis before compositional tests, and replaces the short conclusion with a developed limitations and future-directions section. The appendices are reorganized into separate implementation, related-work, dataset, results and hyperparameter sections. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 changes document-wide title, heading and header styling, boxes the research questions, and adds Figure 1. Table 1 consolidates all six ITA/IEL fine-tuning variants; ablation rows are redistributed between main text and appendix. The compositional tables replace the overall-accuracy column with gain/loss annotations and add an expanded appendix display covering all datasets.

improvement.justification: Explicit checkpoint, initialization, loss and tuning details improve reproducibility; InfLoRA and Figure 1 strengthen empirical assessment, and Section 6 better qualifies the approximations. These support a modest overall improvement. However, the revised empirical-risk assumption does not establish the per-example Hessian positivity still invoked in Section 2.3, and newly listed CLS-prior coefficients remain undefined.
